benefits: Covers the subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration (up to four years) of the respective bachelor's degree programmes at SUTD
Annual allowance of S$6,000 (S$3,000 per academic term)
Priority consideration for the Global Exchange Programme (GEXP)

Travel award of up to S$5,000 for approved overseas programmes including DIVE-related programmes like the Global Innovation Internships (GII), Global Exchange Programmes (GEXP), summer programmes which are at least 4 weeks in duration, as well as selected overseas internships of 16 to 24 weeks
Priority opportunities for leadership development through participation in Fifth Row groups such as the University Ambassador Club
eligibility: Applying for admission to SUTD's undergraduate degree programme
Outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications
Demonstrate strong leadership capabilities and potential
Possess an excellent record in co-curricular and/or community activities
Have the attitude, desire, and potential to make an impact on society
requirements: Achieve and maintain good academic standing; academic performance will be reviewed every term
Complete at least 20 hours of service to the University, e.g. as a student ambassador representing SUTD at publicity talks and receiving guests
Not hold concurrently any other scholarships or grants without the approval of the University
Take up the Tuition Grant Scheme (TGS) from the Singapore Government to enjoy subsidised fees
The scholarship may be withdrawn if the recipient's academic progress or conduct is deemed unsatisfactory; premature termination may trigger repayment on a case-by-case basis

Copy of the front and back of the NRIC (Singapore Citizens) uploaded in the admission application
Academic transcripts and certificates at secondary/junior high and senior high school levels
Up to two referees' contact details plus school or other relevant testimonial(s)/recommendation letter(s)
Declaration of gross monthly household income and answers to the scholarship/financial aid questions in the application

Shortlisted applicants will be notified in due course
SUTD reserves the right not to award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit

coverage: Subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration (up to four years)
Annual allowance of S$6,000 (S$3,000 per academic term)
Travel award of up to S$5,000 for approved overseas programmes
Priority consideration for the Global Exchange Programme and priority leadership-development opportunities in Fifth Row groups

official.duration: The normal duration (up to four years) of the respective bachelor's degree programmes at SUTD
official.description: SUTD frames the Trailblazers Scholarship as a 'highly attractive scholarship that empowers high-performing students who exhibit outstanding potential to lead and make an impact'. It covers subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant for the normal duration of the degree, adds an annual allowance of S$6,000 (S$3,000 per academic term), priority consideration for the Global Exchange Programme, a travel award of up to S$5,000 for approved overseas programmes, and priority leadership-development opportunities through Fifth Row groups. No bond is attached, but recipients must take up the Tuition Grant Scheme.
official.program_type: Leadership and academic merit scholarship for new undergraduate admission applicants (SUTD-administered)

verification.notes: Amounts, benefits, eligibility, terms and application route verified on SUTD's own scholarship page, the SUTD-administered scholarships index, the application guide and the undergraduate admissions page. No separate scholarship deadline, English requirement or study-mode wording is published; fully_funded left false because the page publishes an annual allowance and travel award but never states full coverage of living costs or uses the phrase 'fully funded'.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of SUTD's most comprehensive undergraduate awards for Singapore Citizens: subsidised tuition for the full normal duration of the degree, S$6,000 a year in allowance, priority exchange consideration and up to S$5,000 towards approved overseas programmes, with no bond. There is nothing extra to file - you are considered by flagging scholarship interest inside your SUTD admissions application, and the specific award is announced together with your admission offer. Because awards are decided by competition among eligible applicants and SUTD explicitly reserves the right not to award if no candidate is of sufficient merit, treat your leadership and community evidence as the differentiator, not grades alone. Remember this version is for Singapore Citizens only; permanent residents and international students are directed to the separate SUTD Trailblazers (International) Scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers with top A-Level, polytechnic, NUS High, IB or Year 12 results plus a documented leadership and community record applying to any SUTD bachelor's programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Prepare the SUTD admissions application early and tick the scholarship-interest option plus answer the financial-aid questions, since one missed declaration cannot be corrected later

Line up two referees who have known you academically (school or polytechnic teacher) or professionally (internship or work supervisor) for at least the last six months, secure their consent and collect testimonial letters

Compile transcripts and certificates for secondary and senior high levels plus evidence of leadership, community service, research, internship or entrepreneurship achievements from the last four years
Draft the personal insight responses specifically around leadership and societal impact instead of repeating your CV
Plan a budget for what the award does not touch: hostel, compulsory miscellaneous fees, daily living beyond the S$6,000 allowance and non-approved travel
common_rejection_risks: Failing to indicate scholarship interest inside the admissions application - there is no separate deadline or late route
Strong grades but thin evidence of leadership and co-curricular or community impact
Holding another scholarship or grant concurrently without University approval, which breaches the terms
Letting academic standing slip after the award, since performance is reviewed every term and the scholarship can be withdrawn
Submitting duplicate applications, which SUTD does not process
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel accommodation, compulsory miscellaneous fees, day-to-day living costs beyond the S$6,000 annual allowance, and any travel to overseas programmes that are not on SUTD's approved list (the travel award covers approved programmes only, up to S$5,000).
document_audit: The NRIC front and back must be uploaded in the admission application; partial or blurred scans stall assessment
Referees must have known you for at least the last six months, and you need their consent before listing them
Achievements must fall within the last four years and carry supporting documents such as certificates
Household income is declared as gross monthly figures and must be consistent with anything submitted for financial aid
alerts: The award requires taking up the Singapore Government's Tuition Grant Scheme, so declining the Tuition Grant removes the subsidised-fee benefit
No bond is attached, but 20 hours of University service and term-by-term academic review are binding conditions
Terminating the scholarship early can trigger repayment on a case-by-case basis

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online submission through the SUTD Admissions System with scholarship interest indicated; SUTD assesses admission and scholarship together, shortlists candidates, and names the specific scholarship in the admission offer.

applicant_utility.summary: This is in-year funding for students already inside NTU, not an entry scholarship: you must be a current undergraduate or freshman on subsidised tuition fees, hold no other scholarship and not be on leave of absence, then file one online application during the July window to be considered across the whole donor pool. Award values run from $3,000 to $16,000 for a single academic year, and because some awards are need-based, uploading family ID and income documents in the same application widens what you can be considered for. Say yes to internship interest and to 'All Short Term Scholarships including needs-based scholarships' if you want maximum exposure, and remember that rejecting a shortlist, withholding requested information or missing the interview deems your entire application withdrawn.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Current NTU undergraduates or incoming freshmen on subsidised tuition fees with strong academic results who can document financial need and, where a donor requires it, commit to an internship.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold no other scholarship and will not be on Leave of Absence in any semester of the award year before you apply
Watch for the July window (the AY26-27 window ran 1 to 31 July 2026); freshmen must apply two days after matriculating, so pin that exact date
Gather family members' ID documents (NRIC, passport, student card or birth certificate, with ID numbers masked if you prefer) and income documents matching each member's employment status
Check that every statement you use shows a transaction no older than two months and merge all supporting documents into one file per NTU's checklist
Tick 'Yes' for internship and 'All Short Term Scholarships including needs-based scholarships' to maximise consideration
File the separate bursary application in the same year if you need additional financial support
common_rejection_risks: Applying outside the narrow July window, or freshmen missing the two-days-after-matriculation timing
Holding another scholarship or being on Leave of Absence, both of which are automatic disqualifiers
Leaving internship interest or 'All Short Term Scholarships' unticked, which quietly removes you from donor awards that want interns
Treating the interview as optional: rejecting the invitation, failing to supply requested information or being absent withdraws the whole application
Incomplete applications, late submissions or income documents whose latest transaction is more than two months old
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the one-year $3,000 to $16,000 award: tuition above the subsidised rate, living costs and travel are not designated as covered, and the award lapses after a single academic year.
document_audit: All supporting documents must be combined into a single uploaded document; scattered files delay processing
You may cover or blank off the IC/ID number on ID copies - redact rather than omit the document

Income documents must match each family member's employment-status category on the checklist, including the special cases for full-time tertiary students, pending enlistment and full-time national servicemen
If you are not seeking need-based scholarships, no income documents are needed at all
alerts: The AY26-27 application window (1 to 31 July 2026) has closed and NTU had not published the next cycle's dates at verification, so check the page from June onwards
Awardees must remain active and off Leave of Absence in every semester of the tenure or the scholarship is withdrawn
Shortlist notification arrives only by email by end-September, followed by interviews from August to early October, so monitor the email account you registered
This is an internal NTU award for enrolled or matriculating students; overseas applicants should use NTU's inbound freshman scholarships instead
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application during the July window (freshmen: two days after matriculating) covers the entire pool; NTU matches each applicant to the best donor award they qualify for, emails shortlisted candidates by end-September, and interviews run from August to early October.
